Planar cast shadows

Source: R/depth-cue.R
shadow_3d.Rd

Casts the shadows of a panel's plot layers onto panes of the panel box, for the shadow argument of coord_3d(). Every filled face, stroke and point is projected along the light direction onto the plane of each chosen pane (Blinn 1988) and cut to the pane. The shadows of one layer are painted as one translucent film, the union of their pieces filled once with the nonzero winding rule, so overlapping pieces do not darken twice. The film lies in the pane's plane and is drawn over the pane fill and under its grid lines.

Usage

shadow_3d(on = "floor", alpha = 0.3, colour = "black", light = NULL)

Arguments

on

Panes that receive shadows: "floor", "back", or pane names "xmin" to "zmax".

alpha

Opacity of the shadow film, greater than 0 and at most 1.

colour

Shadow colour.

light

A light_3d() configuration whose direction casts the shadows. NULL uses the light of coord_3d(), or the default light_3d() when that is NULL too.

Value

A shadow configuration for coord_3d().

Details

Strokes cast ribbons of their drawn width and points cast discs of their drawn radius, both measured where the caster lies. Text casts no shadow, and neither do ray-traced layers. A pane receives shadows only when the light reaches it from inside the box, and only while it faces away from the camera, as panes drawn behind the data do. The shadows are vector geometry in every backend: the raster and hybrid backends draw them with the panel furniture.

References

Blinn, J. (1988). Me and my (fake) shadow. IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications 8(1), 82-86.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 25), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 25))
d$z <- exp(-2 * (d$x^2 + d$y^2))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "steelblue", colour = NA) +
  coord_3d(shadow = shadow_3d(light = light_3d(c(1, 1, 3), space = "data")),
    zlim = c(-1, 1))
